title: Free a kitchen drawer jammed by a potato masher
instruction: Open the kitchen drawer all the way, leaving everything in it.
context: Food Preparation Workers (O*NET 35-2021.00; 908,500 employed in 2025, BLS) have the task statement "Carry food supplies, equipment, and utensils to and from storage and work areas." Kitchen utensil drawers are opened all day in homes and kitchens, and a utensil caught under the cabinet's rail is a common way for one to jam. Standing on one end, a potato masher's head is taller than the gap under the face frame's top rail, so the drawer runs out part way and stops hard. Pulling harder only levers the masher up against the rail. A person reaches into the open part of the drawer, rolls the masher onto its fins by the grip, then pulls the drawer out. The masher's pose has to be read from the scene.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. Cabinet: the top-drawer section of a 15 in face-frame base cabinet (sizes estimated from maker photos), 38.1 wide x 33.5 deep x 18.9 tall, fixed on the bench, its face frame's front at x = 37.5, centered on y = 0, with a top panel in place of the countertop. Drawer opening 30.5 x 9.5 under a 5.0 cm top rail whose underside is 8.5 above the drawer's floor. Drawer: a 30.4 deep x 28.0 wide box in 12 mm birch ply (sides 7.0 tall above its floor, floor 3.5 above the bench), 1.7 kg, on 12 in full-extension side-mount slides (30.0 of travel), an overlay front 36 x 12.8 with a 128 mm bar pull (12 mm bar, 2.9 proud of the front, 6.0 up). It starts shut. Masher: an OXO Good Grips Nylon Potato Masher (Target TCIN 80221526): 25.9 long, 136 g, all nylon. Its head is a row of fins 9.9 across (the listing's width), 6.4 deep across the fork and 2.5 long (estimated from maker photos), on a forked neck and a 2.8 thick soft grip in line with it. It lies in the drawer along x, grip toward the robot, on its side with the head standing on one end (10.2 tall) 1 mm in front of the drawer's back wall and the grip's end on the floor (an 8.6 degree slope), its line at y = 4.0. Pulled, the drawer stops at about 21.5 cm open, where the fork meets the rail. Both arms start at the ready pose.
scoring: Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Read each control step from the drawer's slide position, the masher's pose and every arm link's collision hulls; the end of the trial is scored. Flat: the masher's highest point at most 83 mm above the drawer's floor, 2 mm under the rail's underside (lying on its fins it is 65.7 mm tall, on end 102 mm; tilted 10 degrees off its fins 82 mm, 13 degrees 86 mm: the limit is crossed at about 10.6 degrees). 1.0: the drawer out at least 295 mm (stop at 300 mm), the masher flat in it with its whole outline inside the box (within 3 mm), every arm link at least 5 mm from the masher and from the drawer's front and pull, and the masher and drawer still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. 0.5: the masher flat in the drawer and the drawer out at least 280 mm (past the snag at about 215 mm), but not fully out, still held, or still moving. 0.25: the masher flat in the drawer, the drawer out less than 280 mm. 0: anything else, including doing nothing and the drawer left at the snag. Latched 0 for the rest of the trial: the grip more than 30 degrees off level at any moment with the drawer out 205 mm or more (levered up against the rail by a yank at the snag; it starts at 8.6 degrees); any point of the head or fork that the rail catches (higher than the rail's underside at the start) more than 1 mm above the rail's underside while under or in front of the rail (2 mm or more in front of its back face), or any other point (the grip, the fork's front) more than 1 mm above it while under the rail itself, from 2 mm in front of its face to 2 mm in front of its back (forced under the rail); the drawer past 280 mm while the masher is not flat; the masher's lowest point more than 40 mm above the drawer's floor or any of it outside the box at any moment (taken out, even if put back). Opened then shut again scores by the end state (0.25).
reset_notes: Push the drawer in to about 18 cm open (before the snag at 21.5 cm), reach in and stand the masher's head on one end against the back wall with the grip pointing out, then shut the drawer. Under a minute. In simulation the reset is exact.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The masher is a free body jammed and freed by real contact (no joint, capture or scripted jam); its fin head is one solid block and its fork arms straight bars. The drawer is a prismatic joint with the slides' travel as its limit, 3 N s/m joint damping and 20 N s/m drag (assumed) for the ball-bearing slides' rolling resistance. The cabinet is fixed and built from boxes. Friction: wood 0.40/0.30, nylon 0.35/0.30, soft grip 0.8/0.6.
